name: Xai-Xai

queries.query: Xai-Xai Mozambique cadastral parcel map official land registry
queries.result: First-party discovery found the official MOZGIS national geospatial portal and a portal search result for an Xai-Xai hosted service plus the Município da Xai-Xai map service. The exposed layers are administrative, transport, hydrography, facilities, and other base-map layers; no parcel layer was advertised.

queries.query: Xai-Xai Moçambique cadastro predial mapa parcelas oficial registo de terras
queries.result: First-party Portuguese-language discovery found the official municipal Xai-Xai map service and the Ministério da Administração Estatal / PDUL Xai-Xai report. The report describes cadastral coverage differences in urbanized and semi-urbanized areas, but does not expose a public parcel API or safe parcel identities. The official portal service inspection found no parcel/talhão layer.

registryEvidence.custodian: Município da Xai-Xai / official MOZGIS publication; national geospatial portal managed by Agência Nacional de Desenvolvimento Geo-espacial (ADE)
registryEvidence.scopeNote: A first-party municipality-specific public map/service is evidenced. It is not a verified open cadastral parcel service: the hosted Xai_Xai service exposes 16 layers covering facilities, roads, rivers, lakes, administrative boundaries, and related base data, with no parcel/talhão layer. The PDUL report is documentary evidence about varying cadastral conditions, not a parcel endpoint.

boundedResponse.result: Layer 13 returned three administrative OBJECTID values and layer 14 returned two; no parcel geometry or parcel identity was requested or retained.
boundedResponse.crs: EPSG:4326 (service metadata); no parcel CRS applicable

parcelDiscovery.note: No parcel polygon was retained. The exact WUP point was preserved and not shifted; a point hit/miss was not used as a citywide absence test.

uncertainty: The public Xai-Xai service may be incomplete relative to municipal operational data; no authenticated or private route was attempted.
The PDUL report indicates that cadastral geometry and registration coverage varies by urbanization zone, but does not establish publicly queryable citywide parcel coverage.
A FIKANI portal TLS GET failed certificate verification in the local curl environment; no certificate exception was used, and this was not treated as evidence of absence.
No owner, address, titleholder, contact, tax, account, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
